## Source evidence scope

Source acquisition starts **2020-01-01**, inclusive UTC.
Every existing source remains required and enabled. Current snapshots retain older
entities, relationships, internal observations and original dates; this boundary
never clips validity intervals or query/as-of dates. Historical TED packages and
GDELT export windows cannot start earlier. EUR-Lex/DIP observe complete current
catalogues. OffeneRegister stays included with its original historical vintage.
[Every-source scope and recovery policy](SOURCE_DATA_SCOPE.md) governs receipts,
scoped completeness and legacy reconciliation. No production data is purged or
re-ingested by an implementation update.


## Public-officeholder jobs

Submit ingest for `public_offices_<scope>` using the 21 scope codes in
[the BE-56 handoff](GERMAN_PARLIAMENT_MEMBERS.md). Preserve a pre-migration backup;
run the declared 1.4 ontology/DIP data repair explicitly. Historical DIP persons
never certify current membership. The runtime DIP key remains configured through
LIMES_BUNDESTAG_DIP_API_KEY; [public key source/validation](BE56_SOURCES.md) is dated
and does not replace credential configuration. Set nl2cypher_prompt_version=1.1.0
for roster-aware query generation; old explicit pins remain available.
Identity reviews require an archived evidence hash, explicit existing canonical
Person, scoped identifier, note and immutable request_id. They are operator writes;
coverage reads acquire no data. Fixture qualification does not certify production
population, independent legal seat counts or perpetual source availability.

## Reviewed enrichment jobs

Submit `enrich` through POST /operations/jobs with source wikipedia or
yahoo_finance and one to ten `selections`. Each mapping carries an existing
entity_id, a QID and/or symbol plus exchange, evidence_url and rationale. ISIN
and share_class are optional separately reviewed security mappings. A bare ticker
or name never selects a company. `extract_context` defaults to false and is only
accepted for Wikipedia. No consumer read fetches providers. Remote CLI accepts
`--selections` as JSON and `--extract-context`; request IDs preserve job replay.
Inspect acquired sections via GET /entity/ID/enrichment; failed jobs require manual
replay with a new request ID after inspection. Existing source checkpoints advance
only after the entire selected run succeeds; source versions replay idempotently.
Ordinary ingest continues bounded windows through the invocation's safe target;
it does not call one prefix a completed backlog. Failed publishers retain healthy
entries but fail the aggregate coverage result. Source budgets bound work, not
successful notices per hour. A stopped job still needs explicit resubmission.

## Configuration and first startup

Run `python3 tools/init_config.py` as the checkout owner. It creates missing split
files with independent random database/API/operator/backup credentials and grants
read ACLs to UID 7474. Existing files are never read or overwritten by this tool;
ACLs may be refreshed. Install the host `acl` package first. Bind files remain
owned by the operator, without world-read permission or root-owned bind mounts.
Existing volumes must already be owned by UID 7474; an administrator must migrate
older root-owned volumes from a verified backup before startup. Fresh named
volumes inherit the image directory ownership. Set `LIMES_OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
privately in `config/secrets.env` for chat roles. Set
`LIMES_EMBEDDING_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to a separate embeddings-workspace key;
embedding requests and `GET /embeddings/models` never use the chat key. Missing
embedding credentials fail at first embedding use, before any HTTP request.
Keep the chat workspace guardrails unchanged; the embeddings workspace should
allow only the selected embedding model and its serving providers. Embedding
prices come from the embedding catalogue, with the existing logged fallback
when that catalogue or price is unavailable. Set `LIMES_BUNDESTAG_DIP_API_KEY` there for
Bundestag DIP (sent as a header, excluded from source URLs). Public test keys
expire and must be replaced; no key is committed. Keep tokens out
of history, CLI arguments and logs. Use independent consumer, operator and backup
tokens. Back up configuration securely; it is untracked and excluded from images.

After any host edit of `config/*.env`, preserve mode 600 and reapply
`setfacl -m u:7474:r` to each edited file before explicitly restarting services.
File-replacing editors can discard the ACL and cause dotenv permission failures.
Do not put keys in shell arguments or tracked files. See
[BE-51 deployment](EMBEDDING_CREDENTIALS.md) for the operator handoff.

`settings.env` contains tuning; `models.env` contains initial catalogue-validated
pins; `secrets.env` contains credentials. Empty env values are unset. In containers,
`/data/models/models.env` overrides seed pins and atomic tool writes target this
named volume. Model reports use that directory. New worker processes reload pins;
API query contexts refresh pins on their next use. Existing explicit environment values override
file pins. Rootless Docker can administer the stack; any Docker administrator can
start/stop it, while use needs only HTTP credentials.

The base file publishes only `127.0.0.1:8000:8000`. Run base configuration explicitly
with `-f docker-compose.yml`; the auto-loaded development override mounts source
and enables API reload, and must not be used for releases. Use HTTPS termination
forwarding to loopback for remote clients, or an ordinary SSH loopback tunnel.
Keep database and backup-control ports private. The desktop prompts for a session
token; profiles carry names/URLs only. Backup requires the operator session token.

## Operations without Docker membership

Set `LIMES_REMOTE_URL` and `LIMES_OPERATOR_TOKEN` on the client, then run
`venv/bin/limes remote run COMMAND OPTIONS`. Remote mode loads no Neo4j credential
or server configuration. Only HTTPS or loopback HTTP may carry a credential;
redirects are refused. It prints the request UUID before submission. Save that UUID:
reuse `--request-id UUID` with the exact payload after an uncertain response rather
than issuing a new operation. `--no-wait` returns after submission. Resume observation
using `venv/bin/limes remote status UUID --wait`; disconnecting never cancels or
replays work. Output and status are operator-only. A timeout does not imply rollback.
`venv/bin/limes remote cancel UUID` stops one queued or running job without
restarting the worker.

| Command | Parameters |
|---|---|
| ingest | `--source ID` |
| ingest-all | none |
| backfill | `--source ID --days N` (1–36500) |
| reextract | `--version X.Y.Z`, optional `--source ID` |
| select-models | `--stage provisional` or `--stage measured` |
| evaluate | optional `--evaluation extraction`, `resolution` or `nl2cypher` |
| migrate | `--version X.Y.Z` |
| backup | none |
| stamp-embeddings | none |
| public-offices-identify | `--identity-reviews JSON` (1–100 evidence-backed reviews) |

Make operational targets call the same HTTP remote CLI; only `up`/`down` administer
Docker. `make select-models STAGE=measured` and `make evaluate EVALUATION=resolution`
replace the old arbitrary ARGS. Bootstrap structured sources first, stamp embeddings,
then start unstructured backfill. Real measurement can spend money and is an explicit
operator run. Automated verification uses mocked catalogue/inference and gold sets.

Backup returns the named dump only after database recovery. Transfer artifacts using
an administrator-owned volume backup process; the desktop never needs host shell
access to request a dump. Restore on an isolated stopped database with the matching
Neo4j image using `neo4j-admin database load neo4j --from-path=...`; replace the
application volume only after verifying the restored graph. Do not restore into a
running database or overwrite an operator archive as a test.

## Reproducible deployment and evidence

Review and commit changes before deployment. `python3 tools/deploy.py --check`
requires a clean checkout and fetches current main through the baseline guard.
`python3 tools/deploy.py` is an explicit administrator operation: builds from that
commit with full SHA image tags and OCI revision labels, validates non-root image
users, resolves immutable image IDs, starts the base topology with those IDs,
waits for service health, checks running images, and records revision/image IDs and
non-secret seed-config hashes in `deployments/SHA/RUN/record.json`. Configured proxy CA
trust is mounted during API/worker dependency builds in managed environments.

`GET /version` requires a bearer token and exposes the image revision even while
Neo4j is unavailable. Keep the deployment record outside Git with backups. Reuse
its images.yml with the base Compose file to restart the exact saved images; do
not substitute a mutable tag or load the development override. Container image
IDs record the actual artifacts even when an upstream base-image tag later moves.
Archive those images or publish them by digest to retain rebuild/rollback artifacts.
Mutable volumes are intentionally separate from image versioning; pin/evaluation
reports record their own version keys. Redeploying an old image is not a schema
rollback; the ontology downgrade guard still applies.

No code-generation tool or test automatically deploys, tags, commits, pushes,
merges, touches production or makes paid calls. Historical test-instance facts
cannot establish a current release stamp; deploy records are created only by an
actual authorized deployment. CI records JUnit results for every required suite.

## Investigation-driven news acquisition

Default GDELT ingest drains prefixes of at most 96 slots through its safe
publication cutoff within one operation. TED/EUR-Lex bounded incremental windows
also continue through the invocation target; initial historical acquisition is
unfiltered. `ingest-all` attempts all sources and fails its aggregate job if any
source fails. A clean result certifies its requested source windows, not unavailable
historical feed/snapshot coverage. Initial window anchors and active acquisition
windows are durable, so failed retries cannot slide the lookback start.

GDELT `backfill --days N` addresses an older source checkpoint before the fresh
window and continues clean prefixes through the invocation target. Explicit windows
over 96 slots are supported with the composed durable acquisition journal;
standalone adapter use without that journal retains the 96-slot guard. Per-file
byte/row bounds remain. Completed downloads and loads survive an interrupted job;
resubmit the same request explicitly to resume it. Interrupted jobs are never
replayed automatically. A checkpoint already advanced past a gap cannot infer its
lost coverage; preserve evidence and repair the historical window separately.
[Corpus/source audit](CORPUS_INGESTION_RELIABILITY.md) supersedes the old one-prefix-
per-submission instructions in [GDELT/OSM recovery](GDELT_BACKLOG_OSM_LEAVES.md).

OSM exhausted leaf fetch failures are recorded in `failed_leaves` in the durable
acquisition cursor. Eligible siblings continue within the existing 200-call cap;
any failed or pending leaf fails the job before loading or checkpoint advancement.
An explicit resubmission retries incomplete leaves and reuses acquired responses.
Old cursors need no migration; older binaries cannot read the new optional field.

Compressed responses are capped at 16 MiB, decompressed exports
at 128 MiB and rows at 250,000. GLEIF and OffeneRegister archive original compressed
snapshots before bounded normalization chunks (1,000 rows/8 MiB input, 1 MiB per
row). Chunk manifests link original archive hashes/member/row offsets. OffeneRegister
uses historical source `retrieved_at`, never the current clock. GLEIF consolidation
relations distinguish accounting consolidation from ownership. Current TED eForms
and the daily Transparency Register XML are supported with completeness checks.
Malformed/partial records block checkpoint
advancement; successful checkpoints use the covered window endpoint and never
move backward. Failed document loads remain replayable; reextract bypasses the
cache and retracts only extracted evidence after replacement loading succeeds.
No production ingestion is implied by the disposable fixture scenario.

Tracked entities/relations belong to an ongoing investigation that LIMES keeps
informed. The existing worker schedules bounded news-refresh jobs for active
investigations and refreshes current graph names/aliases before setting up DE/EN
public search RSS feeds. Pause stops future cycles; failed/interrupted cycles
require manual replay. Consumer reads never fetch. Operator-only /news tracking
and replay endpoints use the existing API; no extra service is added.

Limits: 256 investigations, four targets/eight feeds per cycle, 2 MiB per response,
25 reports per feed and a 15-minute minimum interval. Original feeds, stable entry
envelopes and acquisition manifests are archived. NewsDocument/NewsClaim artifacts
retain evidence and versions; headlines/snippets are never presented as licensed
agency full text. Publisher access/paywalls are not bypassed. Prompt/schema 2.0.0
keeps attributed proposals/denials separate from factual graph edges. Missing
article text, unknown event time and dependent dispatches stay visible. Acquired
documents form an unreviewed evaluation pool, which operators may annotate.

news-reextract jobs use only archived reports, at most 200 per explicit page,
and emit a next-document cursor when needed. Legacy budget flags remain ignored;
work bounds and job timeout are not monetary spending caps. Production acquisition,
paid quality and deployment are not implied by implementation verification.
